pilot_zone: Foumbot, Noun division, West region, Cameroon

conventions.derived_values: Any value marked 'derived' is plain arithmetic on figures stated in the cited source (unit conversion, per-100 m2 to per-ha, nutrient content from fertilizer grade). Nothing else has been estimated.
conventions.per_100m2_to_ha: 1 ha = 100 x 100 m2, so kg per 100 m2 x 100 = kg per ha

cycle.nursery_days_notes: MINADER S1: 25 to 40 days depending on variety. FAO S12: transplant after 25 to 35 days. NIHORT S14: 4 to 5 weeks. SHEP Kenya S15: 30 to 45 days.
cycle.transplant_to_first_harvest_notes: MINADER S1: 60 to 80 days after planting out. SHEP Kenya S15: Rio Grande 75 to 85 days, hybrids about 75 days. Fovo S2 (Rio Grande, East Cameroon): first fruiting 38 to 51 days after transplanting, depending on fertilization.
cycle.harvest_duration_notes: MINADER S1: harvest spread over 2 to 3 months (60 to 90 days). Tolly and Kamtchouing S5 (Rio, West Cameroon): 4 to 6 harvests at one-week intervals (about 4 to 6 weeks; the 28-day lower bound is derived from 4 weekly harvests).
cycle.total_cycle_notes: MINADER S1 gives 120 to 150 days (sowing to end of harvest). FAO S12 gives a 90 to 150 day total growing period, 90 to 120 days in the field. Tolly S5 gives about 80 days for the production cycle (field). Short-cycle hybrids: Cobra 26 F1 65 to 70 days (GIZ Mali S40), Raja F1 65 to 70 days (Keegoui S9); the cycle definition used by those sources is not stated.

determinate.use: Canning/processing types, plum or elongated fruit (MINADER S1)
determinate.harvest_pattern: Concentrated: 4 to 6 weekly harvests for Rio-type (S5)

indeterminate.harvest_pattern: Extended: 2 to 3 months in the open field (S1); greenhouse hybrids such as Anna F1 harvested over 8 months in Kenya (S15)

varieties_cameroon_sourced.name: Rio Grande
varieties_cameroon_sourced.notes: MINADER recommended, mainly cool dry season (S1). Used in trials in East (S2) and Central (S10) Cameroon. Lowest yield of 3 varieties in Central Cameroon (4.46 t/ha) (S10). Kenya: 18,000 kg/acre potential (S15).

varieties_cameroon_sourced.name: Roma VF
varieties_cameroon_sourced.notes: Hot areas, resistant to Verticillium and Fusarium (S1); 6.05 t/ha in Central Cameroon on-farm trial as 'Roma' (S10)

varieties_cameroon_sourced.name: Cobra 26 F1
varieties_cameroon_sourced.notes: Early, high-yield, disease tolerant, hot dry and cool seasons (S1). 65 to 70 day cycle, 100 to 120 g square firm fruit (Technisem product, GIZ Mali sheet S40)

varieties_cameroon_sourced.name: Rossol
varieties_cameroon_sourced.notes: Highest yield (8.12 t/ha) in Central Cameroon on-farm trial, nematode resistance cited (S10)

varieties_cameroon_sourced.name: Raja F1
varieties_cameroon_sourced.notes: 65 to 70 day cycle, used in Dschang trial 2024 (S9)

varieties_cameroon_sourced.name: Barnum (hybrid)
varieties_cameroon_sourced.notes: Named by a West Cameroon commercial grower, Agribusiness TV story 2016 (S41); low-rigour source

varieties_cameroon_sourced.name: Dona F1, Heinz 1370, Fline, Mecline, Moboline
varieties_cameroon_sourced.notes: Top marketable yields 55 to 68 t/ha in sprayed trial plots, Dschang 1995 (S8)

cycle.varieties_not_found_in_cameroon_sources: Mongal F1, Kiara F1 and Padma were not found in any Cameroon source consulted; not included.
cycle.hybrid_adoption_west: 94% of classified growers (119 of 127) in Foumbot, Bansoa and Dschang used hybrid seed (Titti et al. 2024, S3)

spacing_and_density_by_source.spacing: 80 x 50 cm (staggered 40 to 50 cm in row)

spacing_and_density_by_source.notes: 6,666 to 13,333 plants per acre stated (about 16,500 to 32,900 per ha derived)

planting.seed_rate_notes: MINADER S1 gives no g/ha rate in the text but budgets 3 x 100 g seed bags (300 g) for 1 ha. NAERLS Nigeria S13: 250 to 500 g/ha. SHEP Kenya S15: 40 to 75 g per acre (about 99 to 185 g/ha derived). Hybrid seed is usually sold by seed count; no g/ha found for hybrids in Cameroon.
planting.nursery_sowing_density: 500 seeds per m2 (rows 20 cm apart, 1 seed per cm) (S1)
planting.seedling_at_transplant: About 15 cm tall, 5 to 6 leaves, 5 mm stem diameter (S1); 10 to 13 cm or 4 to 5 leaves (S13)

staking.material: Canes at least 1 m high, bamboo preferred (NIHORT S14). MINADER S1 does not specify material. One West Cameroon grower ties 10 plants per support frame (S41).
staking.stake_cost_notes: MINADER budget has staking labour (10 + 20 person-days) but no stake purchase line. No stake price found.

itinerary.step: Site selection, rotation and soil check
itinerary.timing_basis: No timing given in sources; must precede land preparation
itinerary.description: Avoid plots with Solanaceae in the last 3 years (S15). Where bacterial wilt is present, rotate at least 5 years with cereals; at least 3 years for nematodes (S13). Well-drained light loam, pH 5 to 7 (FAO S12); pH 6.0 to 6.5 (NIHORT S14). Waterlogging raises bacterial wilt risk (S12). Soil analysis should set final fertilizer rates (S15); Titti et al. recommend soil-based fertilization because unregulated synthetic fertilizer use drives preharvest losses (S3).

Manual clearing then avoid burning biomass (MINADER S1 explicitly advises against burning; Ghana FSRP also prohibits burning near tomato fields). Slash-and-burn is therefore not recommended; no source quantifying its effects in Foumbot was found. Herbicide option: glyphosate (Round Up) budgeted at 4 L/ha by MINADER. In Foumbot, 83% of surveyed growers used paraquat and 6% glyphosate (S4, Feb 2020); paraquat is a highly hazardous product and its registration status in Cameroon was not verified.
itinerary.labour_notes: 20 person-days clearing + 6 person-days herbicide treatment (MINADER S1 budget)

itinerary.description: Plough 30 to 50 cm deep without inverting the soil; on slopes, grass strips across the slope (S1). Ridges or beds; double rows 50 cm apart for indeterminate varieties (S1). In Central Cameroon, manual or tractor tillage with stumps removed gave higher yields than no-till with stumps (S10); tractor hire cost in Cameroon not found.
itinerary.labour_notes: 60 person-days ploughing + 30 person-days ridging (manual, MINADER S1)

itinerary.description: 60 m2 nursery per ha for fresh-market tomato (80 m2 for processing types). Disinfect with soil disinfectant or 10 L of boiling water per m2, mulch, rest at least 1 week. Sow 500 seeds/m2 in rows 20 cm apart. Shade structure. Harden seedlings 1 to 2 weeks before transplanting (S15). Seed dressing example: Apron Star 10 g per 2.5 kg seed (S13).
itinerary.labour_notes: MINADER budgets nursery work per m2 (80 m2 x 500 XAF soil prep + 80 m2 x 1,000 XAF disinfection = 120,000 XAF), not in person-days

itinerary.timing_basis: NIHORT S14: organic fertilizer 2 weeks before transplanting; MINADER S1: incorporated at land preparation
itinerary.description: MINADER: 200 to 300 kg organic matter per 100 m2 (20 to 30 t/ha derived) plus 4 kg NPK 10-10-20 per 100 m2 (400 kg/ha derived), incorporated by digging. Organic-only alternative: 30 to 50 t/ha organic matter enriched with 10% fish and bone meal. Trials: poultry manure 10 t/ha + NPK 20-10-10 at 100 g/m2 (1,000 kg/ha) gave the best value-cost ratio (2.49) in East Cameroon (S2); poultry manure 5 t/ha + 150 kg/ha NPK 20-10-10 gave 26.3 t/ha in Dschang (S9).
itinerary.labour_notes: 35 person-days for manure spreading (S2, East Cameroon trial); MINADER has no separate manure line

itinerary.description: Transplant seedlings about 15 cm, 5 to 6 leaves, 5 mm stem at 80 x 50 cm (about 25,000 plants/ha). Gap filling (re-sowing) afterwards.

itinerary.timing_basis: Not stated by MINADER; NIHORT S14 places staking at the peak of the rainy season
itinerary.description: About 25,000 stakes/ha; 2 m stakes (1.6 m above ground) for indeterminate, 1.1 m (0.8 m above ground) for determinate (S1). Bamboo canes at least 1 m (S14). Twine budgeted (1 roll) (S1). Determinate varieties may be left unstaked and mulched in the dry season (S15).

itinerary.timing_basis: MINADER S1: at 15, 30, 50 and 80 days after planting out
itinerary.description: MINADER text: 2 kg NPK 20-10-10 per 100 m2 at each of 15, 30, 50 and 80 days after transplanting (about 8 g per plant per application; 200 kg/ha per application, 800 kg/ha total, derived). MINADER budget additionally lists potassium sulphate 500 kg/ha and calcium nitrate 250 kg/ha (timing not given in text) and puts total 20-10-10 at 1,200 kg/ha, which conflicts with the 800 kg/ha in the text. Comparables: NIHORT 15-15-15 200 to 250 kg/ha split at 3 weeks after transplanting and at fruit set (S14); SHEP Kenya CAN 40 kg/acre at 4 weeks and 80 kg/acre at 8 weeks (S15). West Cameroon growers use DAP, urea, 20-10-10, 13-13-21+S+B+Zn and 15-0-0+26CaO+0.3B; DAP and 13-13-21 were associated with higher preharvest losses (S3).

inputs.unit: kg per application (800 kg/ha total in text; 1,200 kg/ha in budget)
kg per cycle (budget only; split not specified)
kg per cycle (budget only; split not specified)

itinerary.labour_notes: 6 person-days mineral fertilizer spreading (S1); 25 person-days in the East Cameroon trial (S2)

itinerary.step: Calcium supply (blossom end rot prevention) and foliar inputs
itinerary.description: Calcium nitrate 250 kg/ha is budgeted by MINADER (S1); growers in West Cameroon use a 15-0-0 + 26 CaO + 0.3 B product (S3). Liquid organic input Net Eden (N 2.7%, P 2.6%, K 3.0%, Ca 5.2%, Mg 2.5%) at 1 L/ha alone raised yield from 6.5 to 13.6 t/ha in Dschang (S9). No sourced rates were found for foliar fertilizers, biostimulants or the 'vitamins' sold to growers in Cameroon.

itinerary.timing_basis: Daily through the cycle, reduced near the end (S1); upper bound is the end of the MINADER cycle and is indicative
itinerary.description: Water daily at cool hours: 0.5 L per plant per day before fruiting and 1 L per plant per day after fruiting; frequency can drop near the end of the cycle; drip recommended (S1). At 25,000 plants/ha that is 12.5 then 25 m3/ha/day (1.25 then 2.5 mm/day, derived), which is below FAO crop water need: 400 to 600 mm after transplanting (S12), Kc mid-season 1.05 to 1.25. NAERLS Nigeria: irrigate every 5 to 7 days, 15 to 20 times, 400 to 600 mm in total (S13). Foumbot growers pump from streams with motor pumps (S4). MINADER investment: motor pump 200,000 XAF, water reserve points 300,000 XAF, fuel 30,000 XAF, pump maintenance 15,000 XAF per ha.

itinerary.timing_basis: NAERLS S13: hand weeding at 2, 4 and 6 weeks after transplanting; NIHORT S14: first weeding 3 to 5 weeks after transplanting, at least twice
itinerary.description: Hand weeding and earthing up. Weeding time in Central Cameroon trial: 153 to 157 h/ha with stumps removed, 243 h/ha with stumps retained (S10). NIHORT pre-transplant metribuzin 1.0 to 1.5 kg a.i./ha 2 days before transplanting (S14); not reported as a Cameroon practice.

MINADER: general pruning not recommended; on indeterminate varieties remove lower leaves for ventilation (S1). SHEP Kenya: remove side shoots and diseased leaves, sterilize blades with bleach 1:1 (S15).

itinerary.timing_basis: Weekly sprays through the cycle in Cameroon trials (S8) and common farmer practice (S19); end bound indicative
itinerary.description: MINADER first line: monitoring with pheromone and food-bait traps, neem/chilli/garlic/ginger preparation at 4 L/ha (10 L/ha for the CEFRA bio-pesticide recipes); chemicals only if resistance is confirmed: maneb 2 kg/ha, Decis (deltamethrin) 1 L/ha (S1). MINADER budget per ha nevertheless includes mancozeb 80 kg, Ridomil 20 kg (200 x 100 g), Decis 20 L. Dschang trial (S8): Ridomil Plus (metalaxyl + copper oxide) 2.0 kg/ha weekly before flowering, then maneb 1.6 kg/ha weekly after flowering. East Cameroon trial best protocol P1 (S2): 10 x mancozeb 2.5 kg/ha + 5 x lambda-cyhalothrin product 1 L/ha + 5 x second insecticide 1 L/ha. Foumbot growers (S4): lambda-cyhalothrin 100%, chlorantraniliprole 98%, cypermethrin 95%, chlorpyrifos-ethyl 87%, methomyl 80%, imidacloprid 75%, acetamiprid 72%, mancozeb 67%, emamectin benzoate 62%, alphamethrin 23%, thiamethoxam 19%, abamectin 18%; 77% increase frequency at fruiting, 93% ignore preharvest intervals, residues above MRL for lambda-cyhalothrin and cypermethrin. West growers: 91% combine contact and systemic fungicides (S3).

itinerary.sprays_per_cycle_notes: Fungicide applications: 10 in East Cameroon best protocol (S2); weekly spraying in Dschang trial over a March to July or July to November season (S8, count derived as roughly 15 to 17 weeks, indicative). Farmers: weekly spraying most common among Cameroon vegetable growers (S19).
itinerary.labour_notes: MINADER budgets 6 person-days for all fungicide/insecticide treatments (S1); the East Cameroon trial uses 3 person-days per application, i.e. 30 to 33 person-days for 10 to 11 applications (S2)

itinerary.timing_basis: First harvest 60 to 80 days after transplanting, spread over 2 to 3 months (S1)
itinerary.description: Pick by twisting the stalk. Stage: yellow-pink for delayed sale, orange-red for direct sale, bright red for processing (S1). At least one harvest per week (S14); 4 to 6 weekly harvests for Rio-type (S5). Harvest cost in East Cameroon trial: 500 XAF per 85 kg crate (S2).

Rigid crates, boxes or cartons; store in a cool dry place; ash on fruit extends shelf life; processing options: sun-dried slices, concentrate, juice, jam (S1). MINADER budget: 800 crates/baskets at 300 XAF, transport and handling 50,000 XAF/ha. Traditional crate: about 400 g empty, 20 to 25 L, 250 to 300 XAF (S5). A 20 kg crate is the sales unit in the 2024 Dschang study (S9).

minader_text_programme.notes: Mineral fertilizer only, excluding manure; derived from grades (400 kg 10-10-20 = 40-40-80; 800 kg 20-10-10 = 160-80-80)

minader_budget_programme.notes: Derived with standard grades: 20-10-10; K2SO4 50% K2O; calcium nitrate 15.5% N. Budget and text conflict (1,200 vs 800 kg 20-10-10; budget omits 10-10-20).

reference_recommendations.unit: kg/ha as published by FAO for high-yielding varieties (FAO page lists them as N, P, K)
kg/ha, NAERLS Nigeria, plus compost and lime

observed_farmer_use_west_cameroon.finding: Heavy unregulated synthetic use (Type 1, 1,210 kg/ha) had the highest preharvest losses (14%)

trial_results_cameroon.treatment: Poultry manure 2.5 t/ha + Net Eden 0.5 L/ha

input_prices_xaf.period: East Cameroon trial, year not stated (published 2016)

pests_diseases.name: Late blight
pests_diseases.importance: Most severe disease with early blight in the western highlands (S7); caused most damage in the July to November trial in Dschang; marketable yield loss up to 100% when unsprayed (S8)

pests_diseases.name: Early blight
pests_diseases.importance: Main disease with late blight; more severe early in the March to July trial (S8)

pests_diseases.name: Bacterial wilt
pests_diseases.importance: Listed by MINADER; waterlogging increases risk (FAO)
pests_diseases.management: Rotation at least 5 years with cereals (S13); spot treatment with 10% sodium hypochlorite and soil solarization 2 to 3 months (S15); no chemical cure

pests_diseases.name: Fusarium and Verticillium wilts
pests_diseases.agent: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lycopersici; Verticillium spp.
pests_diseases.importance: Listed by MINADER; Fusarium and root rot can cause 90% or more damage (Nigeria S13)
pests_diseases.management: Resistant varieties such as Roma VF (S1)

pests_diseases.name: Fruit flies
pests_diseases.agent: Melon fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae, spelled 'Bacus' in source) and others
pests_diseases.importance: Most prevalent insect pest in the western highlands survey 1993 to 1996 (S7)

pests_diseases.name: Tomato leaf miner
pests_diseases.management: Pheromone traps 4 to 6 per acre (Kenya S15)
active_ingredients: abamectin (all used by Foumbot growers, S4; rates not reported)

pests_diseases.name: Fruit borer / bollworm
pests_diseases.importance: Listed in Nigeria and Kenya guides; caterpillars listed by MINADER

pests_diseases.name: Whiteflies
active_ingredients: thiamethoxam (used by Foumbot growers, S4; rates not reported)

pests_diseases.name: Mites
pests_diseases.importance: Listed by MINADER and SHEP Kenya
active_ingredients: abamectin (used by 18% of Foumbot growers, S4)

pests_diseases.name: Root-knot nematodes
pests_diseases.importance: Listed by MINADER; 10 to 40% losses (Nigeria S13)
pests_diseases.management: Rotation at least 3 years (S13); resistant varieties such as Rossol suggested (S10); carbofuran 3G 30 to 40 kg/ha appears in the Nigerian bulletin but carbofuran is banned in many countries and its status in Cameroon was not verified

pesticide_safety_notes: Foumbot survey (S4, 100 growers, Feb 2020): 100% without protective equipment, 93% ignore preharvest intervals, 56% raise doses, 68% reuse empty containers; lambda-cyhalothrin residues above MRL in all positive samples and cypermethrin in 92.3%. Chlorpyrifos, methomyl and paraquat are widely used despite being highly hazardous; registration status not verified.
labour_notes: Only one complete Cameroon breakdown found: MINADER S1 budget totals 290 person-days/ha (clearing 20, ploughing 60, ridging 30, transplanting 30, gap filling 5, staking 10 + 20, watering 25, fertilizer 6, pesticide 6, herbicide 6, weeding/earthing 15, pruning 15, harvest 40, packaging 2), at 2,500 XAF per person-day, excluding nursery work. Pesticide labour is probably underestimated: East Cameroon trial uses 3 person-days per spray (S2), i.e. about 30 for 10 sprays, plus 35 for manure spreading. Ghana comparison (S16): 35 to 97 unpaid family person-days/ha, hired labour not counted.

faostat_cameroon.notes: FAOSTAT via Our World in Data (FAO 2025 release). The jump from 12.4 to 17.6 t/ha in 2016 suggests a series revision or imputation; MINADER S1 instead cites about 11 t/ha (range 2 to 22) for FAOSTAT 2021, and Tolly S5 cites 11.3 t/ha on 150,000 ha for 2012. Treat the national average as uncertain (11 to 19 t/ha).

yields_t_ha.farmer_rainfed_notes: MINADER rainy-season yield 100 to 250 kg per 100 m2 = 10 to 25 t/ha (S1). On-farm trial Central Cameroon 4.46 to 8.12 t/ha by variety (S10). Unfertilized controls: 6.5 t/ha Dschang 2024 (S9), 1.7 to 5.7 t/ha East Cameroon (S2). West Cameroon farmer survey reports 669 to 1,587 baskets/ha (S3), but basket weight is not given, so it cannot be converted.
yields_t_ha.good_practice_rainfed_notes: Dschang 2024, March to June, manure + mineral: 21.2 to 26.3 t/ha (S9). East Cameroon best protocol with manure + NPK: 23.8 t/ha (S2). Research-plot ceiling: 55 to 68 t/ha for the best varieties sprayed weekly in Dschang 1995 (S8). MINADER general average 20 to 50 t/ha depending on variety (S1).
yields_t_ha.irrigated_dry_season_notes: MINADER dry-season yield 200 to 500 kg per 100 m2 = 20 to 50 t/ha (S1). FAO good commercial irrigated yield 45 to 65 t/ha (S12). Kenya Rio Grande 18,000 kg/acre = about 44 t/ha derived (S15). Ghana irrigated farmers only 5.3 to 14.6 t/ha (S16).

fao_minader_2013_west_chains.chains: Mbouda-Bafoussam-Douala and Foumbot-Bafoussam-Douala, Sept to Oct 2013

post_harvest_loss_detail.notes: Lower bound 6% = transport plus marketing losses on the Foumbot chain (S5, derived sum). Upper bound 40% = overall farm-to-market losses including preharvest (S5, S6, S42).

prices.unit_notes: Cameroon media quote the 'cageot' (crate) without stating its weight. Weights found: a 20 kg crate at 5,500 XAF in Dschang 2024 (S9); an 85 kg crate in an East Cameroon trial (S2); traditional crates of 20 to 25 L volume and about 400 g empty (S5); 15 L and 20 kg buckets in the North-West (S38). Per-kg values are given only where the source gives a weight or a per-kg price; crate prices are kept in price_xaf_per_crate. Converting crate prices to per-kg needs a measured crate weight for Foumbot.

prices.seasonality: Indicative, built from dated observations, no monthly price series found for Foumbot. High or scarcity prices: roughly July to November (peak rains: late blight, fruit rot, bad roads, exports to Gabon and Equatorial Guinea). Examples: Aug 2017 11,000 to 12,000 per crate, Sep to Nov 2017 15,000 in Douala, Oct 2025 12,000 to 15,000 in Yaoundé, late 2025 10,000 to 20,000, mid-Jul 2026 5,800 to 6,500. Low or glut prices: roughly December to March (dry-season irrigated harvests in the West): Dec 2017 Douala flooded, Feb 2021 Bafoussam 1,000 to 4,000, Feb to Mar 2026 1,000 to 2,500. April to June is a transition with sharp rises (May 2025 3,000 to 6,000). Exceptions: Sep 2026 was a glut (Bafoussam 1,000 to 2,000) after regular rains and simultaneous harvests across basins (S22), and 2020 prices collapsed in June because of Covid border closures. Rainy-season price premium: 11,000 to 12,000 vs 7,000 usual (S32). Intra-year range per crate: about 1,000 to 25,000 XAF (S24).
prices.markets: Foumbot (Noun) is the main basin, said to supply close to 40% of national output (MINADER via S22); Titti et al. cite 525,760 t/year for the Foumbot supply chain (S3). Noun department produced 26,829 t in 2010 (Agri-Stat 16, via S39). Flows: Foumbot to Bafoussam to Douala (S5, S6) and to Yaoundé (Mfoundi, Etoudi, Mvog-Mbi, Messassi markets).
prices.exports: Gabon and Equatorial Guinea are the main cross-border buyers (S33, S34, S35, S37); also Chad, Nigeria, Niger, Congo (S32, S34). Mostly informal: only about 120 t of fresh tomato declared exported in 2024 (WITS, via S22). Border closures in 2020 caused a price collapse (S31, S32).

Partial costs only, East Cameroon trial (Rio Grande): crop protection 188,000 to 558,900; fertilization package 1,082,909 to 1,403,018 (manure + NPK + transport + spreading + interest); harvest 22,243 to 100,654
MINADER 2020 tomato rescue plan unit allocations (derived per ha from the 1,000 ha budget): phytosanitary products 425,000 XAF/ha; hybrid seed over 1,000,000 XAF/ha
Unit cost per crate: about 2,700 XAF per crate produced (agronomists and farmer organisations, 2026); break-even 1,500 XAF per crate farm gate (MINADER, 2020)

margins.description: MINADER standard budget, 1 ha, year 1: revenue 3,600,000 (800 crates x 4,500); gross margin over operating costs 1,113,500; net profit after depreciation 943,000. Two campaigns: gross margin 2,227,000, net 1,886,000. Revenue / operating cost = 1.45 (derived); revenue / total year-1 outlay = 1.01 (derived). Crate weight not stated.
East Cameroon trial: net benefit over protection and harvest costs only, best protocol P1: 4,027,526 XAF/ha at 17.06 t/ha and 235 XAF/kg (partial budget, not full margin)
East Cameroon trial: value-cost ratio of fertilization 1.49 to 2.49 (poultry manure 10 t/ha + NPK 20-10-10 best)
Dschang 2024 trial: value-cost ratio 1.23 to 2.02, economic profitability 22.7 to 102.3%; computed values could not be reproduced from the stated 275 XAF/kg
Crate-level margin 2026: production cost about 2,700 XAF per crate; at 1,000 XAF per crate in glut the producer loses 1,700 XAF per crate before transport
Retail margin 2020: retailers selling at 2,500 XAF per crate earn about 30% after expenses
Nigeria comparable: 2.93 naira returned per naira invested within 4 months (NIHORT)

climate.temperature_notes: FAO S12: optimal mean daily 18 to 25 C, nights 10 to 20 C; above 25 C with high humidity and wind yields drop; nights above 20 C with high humidity and low sunshine cause excess vegetative growth and poor fruiting. NAERLS S13: optimum 22 to 26 C day, 14 to 16 C night; flowers drop and fruit set is poor above 32 C day or night; fruit set can fail when days exceed 29.4 C and nights 22.2 C. NIHORT S14: optimum 21 to 25 C.
climate.soil: Well-drained light loam, pH 5 to 7 (S12); pH 6.0 to 6.5 (S14); moderately salt sensitive, 0% loss at ECe 2.5, 50% at 7.6 (S12)
climate.heavy_rain_sensitivity: Late blight and early blight are the main constraints; untreated wet-season crops can lose up to 100% of marketable yield (S7, S8). Abundant rain causes rapid fruit rot and supply shortages (S33). MINADER yields: rainy season 10 to 25 t/ha vs dry season 20 to 50 t/ha (S1). High humidity increases pests, diseases and fruit rot (S12).

foumbot_climate.notes: February mean maximum 32.2 C reaches the NAERLS fruit-set limit; July to September are the coolest and wettest (highest late blight pressure).

climate.best_planting_periods_west_highlands: MINADER: sowing March to April and September on the high plateaux (S1). Dschang trials used March to July and July to November seasons; late blight was worst in July to November (S8). Foumbot growers: 51% prefer the dry season, about 40% grow in both seasons, 9% rainy season only; dry-season crops are irrigated from streams with motor pumps (S4). Practical reading for Foumbot (single rainy season): a September sowing puts the harvest in the December to February dry season under irrigation, with higher yields but glut prices; a March sowing gives a rainy-season crop with high disease pressure that is harvested around June to August, when prices start to rise.

confidence_notes: HIGH: technical itinerary skeleton and 1 ha budget (MINADER S1, but internal text vs budget conflicts on NPK 800 vs 1,200 kg/ha and on pesticide quantities); climate thresholds (FAO S12, NAERLS S13); pesticide use pattern in Foumbot (S4); late blight as the dominant rainy-season risk (S7, S8). MEDIUM: yields (MINADER per-100 m2 ranges; few on-farm measurements in the West; FAOSTAT Cameroon series looks revised or imputed after 2015, 19.4 t/ha in 2024 vs about 11 t/ha cited by MINADER); post-harvest losses (2013 studies, 34 to 40% farm to market, about 6 to 7% after harvest on the Foumbot chain); crate prices (many dated press observations but no monthly series, and no stated crate weight except 20 kg in S9). LOW or MISSING: crate weight standard in Foumbot (null; 20 kg in Dschang 2024, 85 kg in an East trial); farm-gate price series for Foumbot itself (null); foliar fertilizer and biostimulant ('vitamin') products and rates (null); stake purchase price and tractor ploughing cost (null); full cost studies other than MINADER (Keegoui gives totals 3.0 to 3.6 M XAF/ha without breakdown); labour per operation from field surveys (only the MINADER budget, 290 person-days/ha, likely underestimating spraying); spray counts per cycle in farmer practice (only 'weekly' and 'more at fruiting'); export volumes to Gabon and Equatorial Guinea (informal, undocumented). Mongal F1, Kiara F1 and Padma were not found in Cameroon sources. Sources not readable: PMC full text of Titti et al. 2024 (captcha; the ResearchGate version was used), Europe PMC (rate-limited). Recommended field work for the March 2027 pilot: weigh Foumbot crates, log weekly farm-gate prices at Foumbot and Bafoussam, record spray counts and labour per operation.
